counterargs.read: The weight of the evidence at this hour is incomplete rather than confirmatory. Korea's selloff is real and complete -- that's not in question -- but it's one data point, and the framework's own transition rules require Group A (duration stress) plus Group B (market-functioning) or Group C (credit) to confirm a regime shift. Group A is technically active again (30Y > 5.5%), Group B is unclear pending MOVE's refresh, and Group C (credit) shows zero stress on stale data. The Treasury auction/demand backdrop hasn't changed either. The right read is caution, not confirmation: treat this as financial conditions re-tightening at the margin with one genuine regional risk-off data point (Korea), and wait for the 9:30am ET US open to see whether credit and equities corroborate or fade it.

treasury_auctions.narrative: The 7Y (91282CRM5, Sep 24) settled decently on the metrics that matter most for dealer stress: BTC 2.42 and dealer take-down 10.76%, both roughly in line with the two comparable 7Y prints in the ledger (Aug 27: BTC 2.50/dealer 10.84%; Jul 28: BTC 2.49/dealer 11.7%). But indirect demand was again soft at 49.13% -- below both those comps (53.72%, 63.0%) and in the same range as the Sep 22 2Y (49.27%) and Sep 23 5Y (46.98%). That makes three straight Note auctions with thinning indirect (often foreign/end-investor) demand, even though only the 5Y also showed elevated dealer take-down. The module holds at EARLY WARNING: this is not a third weak print on every metric (no escalation to Intermediation Stress), but it is not a clean auction either (no downgrade to Healthy). Separately from the auction story, US10Y and US30Y kept selling off into today's session (+11.1bp/+11.7bp since the prior run), with the 30Y crossing the 5.5% long-end stress line for the first time and MOVE spiking a further +9.6% to 104.58. Funding remains normal (SOFR-IORB -2bp, repo_confirmation false) and credit is calm, so this stays short of Intermediation Stress. The next test is the H.8 bank-demand read today and whether credit or equities start reacting to the long end above 5.5%.

The Treasury-demand story is exactly where it was -- three straight thin-indirect Note auctions, module at Early Warning, no new print this weekend to move it -- and a new H.8 vintage shows bank demand ticking down a modest -0.19% w/w. Treat 'Long-End Stress Confirmed' as no longer active on today's levels while keeping the underlying auction-demand and bank-demand softness on watch.
